question: As per the report of the National Rubber Policy 2019, India is the __________ largest producer of Natural Rubber in the world.
solution:
The correct answer is __**sixth**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India is the **sixth largest producer of Natural Rubber** in the world as per the National Rubber Policy 2019.
 
• Natural rubber is a critical raw material used in various industries including automotive, defense, and aviation.
 
• The rubber industry in India significantly contributes to the economy, providing employment to millions of people.
 
• Kerala is the leading state in India for natural rubber production, contributing about 78% of the country's total output.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Rubber Policy 2019**

 
 
• The National Rubber Policy 2019 was introduced by the Indian government to address issues related to the production, consumption, and export of natural rubber in India.
 
• The policy aims to promote the sustainable development of the rubber sector, ensuring the welfare of rubber growers.
 
• It encompasses various aspects such as planting material, cultivation practices, and processing technologies to improve productivity and quality.
 
 
 
• **Natural Rubber**
 
 
• Natural rubber is an elastic hydrocarbon polymer derived from the latex of rubber trees (Hevea brasiliensis).
 
• It is used in the production of numerous products including tires, footwear, and medical devices due to its high elasticity, resilience, and waterproof properties.
 
• Natural rubber is distinct from synthetic rubber, which is produced from petroleum-based monomers.
 
 
 
• **Kerala's Role in Rubber Production**
 
 
• Kerala is the top rubber-producing state in India, with its favorable climate and soil conditions ideal for rubber tree cultivation.
 
• Approximately 90% of India's natural rubber plantations are located in Kerala.
 
• The state's rubber plantations not only contribute to the economy but also play a crucial role in providing employment to rural communities.
